newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent slides, other N.Sea crudes steady.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent slides, other N.Sea crudes steady.

text.p: North Sea crude oil premiums were steady on Monday as Dated Brent continued its slide versus November paper, traders said.

December IPE Brent futures gained 28 cents on the day to $24.50 per barrel by 1848 GMT, but the Nov/Dec spread came under pressure from weak demand for physical Brent, easing by eight cents to +28 cents.

Dated Brent fell 10 cents to trade twice at Dec -6 cents. Both of these cargoes were bought by Stasco last week. One was sold to a Shell affiliate and the other was previously swapped with a trader for Nigerian crude, dealers said.
Traders said prices were coming back into line with fundamentals after Stasco withdrew its support for Dated Brent prices on Friday last week.
Other N.Sea crudes were steady on Monday, illustrated by an Oseberg sale at Dated Brent +31 cents.
In the Mediterranean, Urals continued under pressure with even sellers expecting the next cargo to trade around dated Brent -85/80 cents.
"Margins are O.K. but not as good as they were. The refiners all came out and covered themselves when the margins were great so no-one needs to buy until the latter half of the month.
The sellers are coming down to our levels," one refiner said.
Nigerian premiums were also suffering from falling refining margins. A Qua Iboe on the water was still unsold and might go to the U.S., and two November 10-20 loaders were also unsold.
Other Nigerian offers included one Forcados in the third decade, two Bonny Light and a Brass River.
